works/rule-of-benedict/summary: Seventy-three chapters ordering a community under an abbot: the Divine Office, lectio divina, manual work, obedience, humility, hospitality and stability.
works/rule-of-benedict/significance: The basic rule of Western monasticism for fifteen centuries.
works/guigo-ladder-of-monks/summary: A letter describing four rungs of spiritual exercise: lectio, meditatio, oratio, contemplatio.
works/guigo-ladder-of-monks/significance: Classic definition of lectio divina, revived in the 20th century.
works/bonaventure-journey-of-the-mind/ti: The Soul’s Journey into God (Itinerarium mentis in Deum)
works/bonaventure-journey-of-the-mind/su: Written on Mount La Verna, it traces an ascent through creation, the soul and the divine names to ecstatic union through the crucified Christ, modelled on Francis’s vision of the seraph.
works/bonaventure-journey-of-the-mind/si: Synthesis of Franciscan affective mysticism and scholastic theology.
works/cloud-of-unknowing/summary: Anonymous guide to contemplation teaching the reader to place created things beneath a "cloud of forgetting" and to reach toward God in the "cloud of unknowing" with a naked intent of love, perhaps using a single short word.
works/cloud-of-unknowing/significance: Classic of English apophatic mysticism and the source of Centering Prayer.
works/imitation-of-christ/title: The Imitation of Christ (De imitatione Christi)
works/imitation-of-christ/summary: Four books of counsel on the interior life, inward consolation and the Eucharist, urging humility, contempt of vain learning and union with Christ.
works/imitation-of-christ/significance: The defining book of the Devotio Moderna and one of the most translated Christian books.
works/ignatius-spiritual-exercises/summa: A four-week programme of meditations, contemplations of the Gospels and rules for discernment of spirits, to be given by a director to a retreatant.
works/ignatius-spiritual-exercises/signi: Foundation of Jesuit formation and of the modern retreat; approved by Paul III in 1548.
works/teresa-interior-castle/summary: Describes the soul as a castle of seven dwelling places through which one journeys by prayer toward spiritual marriage with God at the centre.
works/teresa-interior-castle/significanc: Classic map of the stages of prayer; Teresa was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1970.
works/john-cross-dark-night/title: The Dark Night of the Soul
works/john-cross-dark-night/summary: Commentary on John’s poem "On a dark night" describing the passive purifications of sense and spirit by which God draws the soul to union.
works/john-cross-dark-night/significance: Gave Christian spirituality the language of the "dark night".
works/baxter-saints-everlasting-rest/sum: Treatise on heaven with detailed directions for daily "heavenly meditation", engaging understanding, affections and imagination.
works/baxter-saints-everlasting-rest/sig: The classic manual of Puritan meditation, reprinted for two centuries.
works/molinos-spiritual-guide/summary: Guide to interior recollection and passive contemplation through annihilation of self-will.
works/philokalia/summary: Anthology of texts by some thirty-six authors from the 4th to the 15th century on watchfulness, the Jesus Prayer and the purification of the heart, compiled by Nicodemus and Macarius of Corinth.
works/philokalia/significance: Sparked a hesychast revival in Greece, Romania and Russia (Slavonic Dobrotolubiye, 1793).
works/way-of-a-pilgrim/title: The Way of a Pilgrim (Otkrovennye rasskazy strannika)
works/way-of-a-pilgrim/summary: Anonymous first-person narrative of a Russian wanderer who learns from a starets and the Philokalia to pray the Jesus Prayer unceasingly. First printed at Kazan in 1881 (circulating in manuscript earlier).
works/way-of-a-pilgrim/significance: Popularised the Jesus Prayer in Russia and, in translation, worldwide.
works/wesley-sermon-means-of-grace/summa: Defends prayer, searching the Scriptures and the Lord’s Supper as ordinary channels of grace against Moravian "stillness" teaching that seekers should wait without using ordinances.
works/wesley-sermon-means-of-grace/signi: Classic statement of Methodist spiritual discipline.
works/keating-open-mind-open-heart/summa: Manual of Centering Prayer: choosing a sacred word as a symbol of consent to God’s presence and returning to it when distracted.
works/keating-open-mind-open-heart/signi: Main text of the Centering Prayer movement.
works/carmina-gadelica/summary: Collection of prayers, blessings and charms gathered orally in the Scottish Highlands and Islands by Alexander Carmichael, with English translations.
works/carmina-gadelica/significance: Main source of the modern "Celtic spirituality" revival; scholars debate how far Carmichael polished the texts.
works/luther-simple-way-to-pray/summary: Letter to his barber Peter Beskendorf showing how to pray through the Lord’s Prayer, the Ten Commandments and the Creed, letting each phrase become a "garland" of instruction, thanksgiving, confession and petition.
works/luther-simple-way-to-pray/signific: A model of Word-centred Protestant prayer.
works/abelard-sic-et-non/summary: A collection of 158 questions on which patristic authorities appear to contradict one another, with a prologue giving rules for reconciling them (attending to context, vocabulary, authenticity).
works/abelard-sic-et-non/significance: Taught Western schools to treat authorities critically and dialectically, preparing the quaestio method of scholasticism.
works/lombard-sentences/title: Four Books of Sentences (Sententiae in IV libris distinctae)
works/lombard-sentences/summary: Systematic compilation of patristic and early medieval opinions arranged in four books: God and the Trinity; creation and sin; the incarnation and virtues; sacraments and last things.
works/lombard-sentences/significance: The standard theology textbook of the medieval universities for four centuries; Aquinas, Bonaventure, Scotus, Ockham and Luther all lectured on it.
works/luther-disputation-scholastic-theo: Ninety-seven theses (September 1517) attacking the nominalist theology of Gabriel Biel and the use of Aristotle’s ethics in theology, insisting that the will is bound without grace.
Shows that Luther’s break was first a break with late-medieval scholastic method, weeks before the Ninety-five Theses.
works/perkins-golden-chaine/summary: A Latin (Armilla aurea, 1590) and English (1591) exposition of Reformed theology arranged as a "chain" of the causes of salvation and damnation, with a famous fold-out chart.
works/perkins-golden-chaine/significance: Defined the Puritan union of predestinarian doctrine and practical divinity.
works/turretin-institutes/title: Institutes of Elenctic Theology (Institutio theologiae elencticae)
works/turretin-institutes/summary: Three volumes (1679-85) of disputed questions defending Reformed orthodoxy point by point against its opponents.
works/turretin-institutes/significance: Summit of Reformed scholasticism; the Princeton textbook into the 1870s.
works/spener-pia-desideria/summary: A preface to a postil of Johann Arndt that diagnosed the decline of Lutheran church life and proposed six reforms: wider use of Scripture in small groups, the priesthood of all believers, practice over knowledge, charity in controversy, reform of theological training and edifying preaching.
works/spener-pia-desideria/significance: Programme of German Pietism and an early model of small-group renewal.
works/toland-christianity-not-mysterious: Argues that true religion contains nothing contrary to reason nor above it, and that "mysteries" were introduced by priestcraft.
Opened the English Deist controversy; condemned by the Irish Parliament in 1697.
works/kant-religion-bounds-reason/title: Religion within the Bounds of Mere Reason
works/kant-religion-bounds-reason/summar: Reinterprets original sin as radical evil, Christ as the archetype of moral perfection and the Church as an ethical commonwealth.
works/kant-religion-bounds-reason/signif: The most influential philosophical reduction of Christianity to moral religion; it provoked a censorship order from the Prussian king.
works/schleiermacher-on-religion/title: On Religion: Speeches to its Cultured Despisers
works/schleiermacher-on-religion/summary: Five speeches to Romantic intellectuals arguing that religion is neither metaphysics nor morality but "sense and taste for the infinite", a feeling and intuition of the universe.
works/schleiermacher-on-religion/signifi: Founding manifesto of liberal Protestant theology.
works/ritschl-justification-reconciliati: The Christian Doctrine of Justification and Reconciliation
Three volumes (1870-74) presenting Christianity as an ellipse with two foci: redemption through Christ and the ethical Kingdom of God.
Charter of the Ritschlian school that shaped Harnack and the social gospel.
works/tillich-systematic-theology/summar: Three volumes (1951-63) organised by the method of correlation: reason and revelation, being and God, existence and the Christ, life and the Spirit, history and the Kingdom.
works/tillich-systematic-theology/signif: The fullest existentialist-ontological system of 20th-century Protestant theology.
works/lossky-mystical-theology/title: The Mystical Theology of the Eastern Church
works/lossky-mystical-theology/summary: Presents apophatic theology, the Trinity, the essence-energies distinction and deification as one mystical-dogmatic whole.
works/lossky-mystical-theology/significa: Shaped Western perceptions of Orthodoxy and the neo-patristic school.
works/de-lubac-surnaturel/summary: Historical study arguing that the patristic and Thomist tradition knew no "pure nature" sealed off from grace; humanity has a natural desire for the vision of God.
works/de-lubac-surnaturel/significance: Lightning rod of the nouvelle théologie dispute and the encyclical Humani Generis (1950).
works/aeterni-patris/summary: Encyclical urging the restoration of Christian philosophy "according to the mind of the Angelic Doctor", Thomas Aquinas.
works/aeterni-patris/significance: Made neo-Thomism the official framework of Catholic seminaries until Vatican II.
works/lindbeck-nature-of-doctrine/summar: Contrasts propositional, experiential-expressive and cultural-linguistic theories of doctrine and argues for the last.
works/milbank-theology-and-social-theory: Theology and Social Theory: Beyond Secular Reason
Genealogical critique of secular social theory as a rival theology, ending with the Church’s "ontology of peace".
works/cone-black-theology-and-black-powe: Argues that Black Power, the struggle of Black people for liberation, is Christ’s central message to 20th-century America.
works/ruether-sexism-and-god-talk/summar: A feminist systematic theology that tests every doctrine by the full humanity of women.
works/williams-sisters-in-the-wilderness: Builds a womanist theology from the Hagar narratives and Black women’s experiences of survival, surrogacy and quality of life.
works/mbiti-african-religions-and-philos: Survey of the religious worldview common to many African peoples, its concepts of God, spirits, time and community.
Made African traditional religion a partner for Christian theology.
works/koyama-waterbuffalo-theology/summa: Essays from Thailand urging a theology that speaks to the farmer and his water buffalo, attentive to Buddhist culture and the slowness of love.
works/koyama-waterbuffalo-theology/signi: A landmark of Asian contextual theology.
works/yong-spirit-poured-out-work/title: The Spirit Poured Out on All Flesh
works/yong-spirit-poured-out-work/summar: A pneumatological systematic theology drawing on global Pentecostalism.
works/yong-spirit-poured-out-work/signif: A key text of the academic Pentecostal theology movement.
works/nicene-creed-325/summary: The original creed of the Council of Nicaea, confessing the Son ‘begotten of the Father, the only-begotten, that is, of the essence of the Father… of one substance (homoousios) with the Father’, with anathemas against Arian phrases.
works/nicene-creed-325/significance: The first creed issued by an ecumenical council and the foundation of all later Trinitarian orthodoxy.
works/niceno-constantinopolitan-creed/su: The expanded creed associated with the Council of Constantinople (381), read at Chalcedon (451). It adds that the Spirit is ‘the Lord and Giver of life, who proceeds from the Father, who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified’ and confesses ‘one holy catholic and apostolic Church’.
works/niceno-constantinopolitan-creed/si: The most widely shared creed in Christianity, recited in the liturgy of Orthodox, Oriental, Catholic, Anglican, Lutheran and many other churches (in the West with the Filioque).
works/athanasian-creed/summary: A Latin creed, probably from southern Gaul c. 440–540, setting out the Trinity (‘we worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity; neither confounding the persons, nor dividing the substance’) and the incarnation, with damnatory clauses.
works/athanasian-creed/significance: Used in Western liturgy and accepted by Lutheran (Book of Concord) and Anglican (Thirty-Nine Articles) confessions; not used in Orthodox liturgy.
